description: Representation-native robustness and elastic recovery through a hard contact impact. The system's native stable-identity body falls under native gravity onto the system's own released floor/boundary using a soft elastic setting from the released parameter surface, deforms substantially at impact (a deformation gate makes a too-gentle run INVALID rather than a cheap PASS), and must then recover: the state stays finite throughout, identity/count never changes, transient shape error stays bounded (no runaway), and by the tail of the rollout the median shape error returns below a recovery bound. Unlike C5, which demands near-rigid transport fidelity at every frame, C8 deliberately drives the representation through large deformation and grades survival and recovery.

pass_criteria.quantity: finiteness, bounded transient deformation, and tail recovery of stable-identity shape metrics through impact

provenance.reference_formula: peak area_rel_error_p95 >= min_peak_area_p95 (impact actually deformed the body); edge_rel_error_p95 <= transient_edge_p95_max at every frame; min over the last tail_frac of frames of edge_rel_error_median <= tail_edge_median_max and of area_rel_error_median <= tail_area_median_max (elastic recovery)
regime_assumptions: elastic constitutive setting from the released parameter surface (an inelastic material cannot recover and correctly fails)
the floor is part of the system's released pipeline
stable identity: the same physical element keeps the same index in every frame
the recovery bound uses the best-recovered frame in the tail because the body may still be oscillating at the final checkpoint
provenance.notes: Frozen v1. Submission contract is triangle_metrics.csv exactly as SPEC 2.6. A natural controlled fault is running the same drop with a released inelastic material (e.g. sand): the impact gate still passes but the tail recovery bounds fail because plastic flow never returns the shape to rest.
